issues.description: The problem statement text requires the Farm to use a Set (HashSet) to store unique animals, but the UML diagram in the same problem statement shows animals: List<Animal>, and the reference solution implements animals as a List backed by an ArrayList. This mismatch (List vs Set) across the UML, the textual requirements, and the solution creates confusion about the intended collection type and uniqueness constraint and may block or mislead students implementing the Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended collection type explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and keep the textual instruction), and change the reference solution to use Set<Animal> and initialize a new HashSet<> in the no-arg constructor (also update getter/setter signatures to use Set), or (B) change the textual requirement to allow a List and remove the uniqueness/HashSet requirement so the UML, text, and solution consistently use List/ArrayList.
